body:
> Using Control's `find_valid_focus_neighbor()` doesn't find the appropriate neighbor.
> 
> I would expect the behavior to match the focus shifting displayed when using the default UI input actions.
> 
> Here's an example of code I expected to mirror the default behavior but doesn't:

You're calling `find_valid_focus_neighbor()` on the parent GridContainer (which has the example script attached), instead of on the currently focused control.

Changing your `_handle_action` method in the MRP like this makes it work as expected AFAICT:
```gdscript
func _handle_action(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	var current_focus: Control = get_viewport().gui_get_focus_owner()
	if not current_focus:
		return
	
	var next_focus: Control
	
	if event.is_action_pressed("ui_ext_left"):
		print("left")
		next_focus = current_focus.find_valid_focus_neighbor(SIDE_LEFT)
	elif event.is_action_pressed("ui_ext_right"):
		print("right")
		next_focus = current_focus.find_valid_focus_neighbor(SIDE_RIGHT)
	elif event.is_action_pressed("ui_ext_up"):
		print("up")
		next_focus = current_focus.find_valid_focus_neighbor(SIDE_TOP)
	elif event.is_action_pressed("ui_ext_down"):
		print("down")
		next_focus = current_focus.find_valid_focus_neighbor(SIDE_BOTTOM)
	
	if next_focus:
		print(next_focus)
		next_focus.grab_focus()
```

Hence I'm closing this as not a bug (if I've missed something / there's still some issue then please clarify further, the issue could be reopened).
Yep, that was the issue. It makes total sense now that I see it. Thank you so much.
